inference: The maṅgala names its object twice: the formed world transcended, the shining self whose power does not end.
premises: Homage to the world-formed, beyond the world.
To ever-divine-shining, self with unending power.
question: What is first worshipped?
speaker: Poet (maṅgala)

inference: Identity and non-identity both refused: neither you alone nor I alone, nor both — only homage where the question lands.
premises: You alone are you; I alone am I; you alone are; I am not at all.
I and you as both are not: where homage, homage, homage.
question: Who are you, who am I?
speaker: Poet (identity)

inference: Seeking finds no self to see: whatever is seen is you alone — the sought turns out to be the seer.
premises: Sought inside the body by me always — you as self, and never seen is the self.
Whatever is seen is you alone, that.
question: What is found inside?
speaker: Poet (seeking)

inference: Recognition declared both ways: seen as self, homage goes to you and to me — knower and known each honored.
premises: Of your devotee who well knows your form, now again.
Having seen you as the self's form: to you homage, to me homage.
question: What does the devotee declare?
speaker: Poet (recognition)

inference: Method questioned to its root: given your magic-nature, what instrument, what place, what origin could dissolving have.
premises: What going-finesse, what to be done, thus, from the root.
Of yours, made of your magic power: by what, in what, whence the dissolving.
question: What finesse remains?
speaker: Poet (method-question)

inference: Non-duality asserted, difference explained away: what looks like abiding difference is only the wish to grasp samādhi.
premises: I, you; you, I — thus: no duality of us anywhere.
Only the wish to grasp samādhi: abiding of difference is just that.
question: Is there duality?
speaker: Poet (non-duality)

inference: Speech finds no room in you: if even I-and-you-talk cannot stay, whence a world of words.
premises: You-I and so-on, so endless, ever in you, never find a place.
Words, then — whence the world.
question: Where do words go?
speaker: Poet (speech)
uncertainties: Print variant so yamityādi nūnaṃ tāni noted; edition so'nantāni kept.

inference: Enough of talking difference: devotion chewed to sap leaves all as one, at peace — and even saying so is shy.
premises: Enough of difference-talk: from chewing the sap of devotion to you.
All this is one, at peace — even to say so is shy.
question: What is enough?
speaker: Poet (enough)

inference: Expansion holds all three; withdrawal holds none: being and nonbeing of you, me, world turn on your play.
premises: Your own form expanding — you and I and the whole world.
Born its withdrawal — neither you nor I nor world indeed.
question: What when you expand, what when you withdraw?
speaker: Poet (expansion)

inference: States held as own rays: shining by own will like an actor, yet partless in truth.
premises: Waking-dream-deep-sleep and the rest, holding as own rays.
By own will you shine like an actor — partless, yet in truth.
question: Who shines like an actor yet stays partless?
speaker: Poet (actor)
uncertainties: Print naTavan kept byte-true (probable slip for naṭavat actor-like); gloss follows sense.

inference: Waking and sleep derived: his waking yours, his rest yours — hence all is of your nature, real-and-unreal.
premises: From your waking, his waking; from your sleep, his rest.
Hence all is of your nature: the world as real-unreal.
question: Whose is all this?
speaker: Poet (derivation)

inference: Rites exhausted at the start: tired tongue, tired mind — meditation with no form to hold, name with no quality to name.
premises: The tongue is tired in your name; the mind is tired in remembering you.
Of the formless, what meditation; of the qualityless, what name.
question: What use are rites for the formless?
speaker: Poet (exhaustion)

inference: The kutaḥ series opens: summoning, seating, washing, sipping — each rite asked where, for whom without place.
premises: Where is summoning for the full; where a seat for the all-based.
Foot-water and respects for the clean; sipping for the pure.
question: Where is the seat for the all-based?
speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)

inference: Adornment rites interrogated: no bath, no garment, no scent, no jewel where stainless, world-full, unanointed, lovely.
premises: What bath for the stainless; what garment for the world-bellied.
What scent for the unanointed; what jewel for the lovely.
question: What bath, garment, scent, jewel?
speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)

inference: Offering rites interrogated: thread, flowers, incense, lamp — each without a receiver.
premises: Sacred thread for the propless; flowers for the desireless.
Incense for the noseless, lamp for the eyeless — what use.
question: What thread, flowers, incense, lamp?
speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)
uncertainties: Print variant apraṇasya (for-breathless) noted; edition aghrāṇa (noseless) kept.

inference: Honorific rites interrogated: food, betel, circling, bowing — all without a needy recipient.
premises: Food-offering for the ever-content, betel for the Lord — whence.
Circumambulation for the endless, obeisance for the non-dual — whence.
question: What offering, circumambulation, obeisance?
speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)

inference: Even praise interrogated: lights for the self-shining, hymn for the unspeakable — enjoined how.
premises: Whence waving-lights for the self-shining Lord.
How is a hymn enjoined for the Veda-unspeakable.
question: How is the hymn enjoined?
speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)

inference: Farewell and fire-offering interrogated: no going out for the full, no difference for the fire.
premises: How is sending-off for the full, inside and out.
And how is oblation for the difference-free, everywhere.
question: How sending-off, how oblation?
speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)

inference: Closing rites interrogated: fee, drink, dismissal, pardon — none owed where full, content, everywhere, unseen.
premises: Where is the fee for the full; libation for the ever-content.
Dismissal for the all-pervading; pardon for the unseen.
question: What fee, libation, dismissal, pardon?
speaker: Poet (kutaḥ)

inference: The answer after twenty negations: nondual mind yoked to the Lord of all, in every state, always — that is the highest worship.
premises: Just so, indeed, the highest worship, in all states, always.
With nondual mind, yoke the mind to God as Lord of all.
question: What then is worship?
speaker: Poet (seal)
